title: Staking rewards currently bypass the revenue waterfall and are paid from SKY reserves until those run down
content:
A.2.3.1.4.1 states that pending activation of USDS Staking Rewards, "no Step 4 Capital is allocated to SKY Staking Rewards." Instead they are "funded from SKY token reserves held by the Protocol Treasury via the Vesting Stream Contract... distributed at a rate equivalent to fifty percent (50%) of Step 2 Capital from the prior Monthly Settlement Cycle," with the rate set monthly by the Core Facilitator in consultation with the Core Council Risk Advisor "using the prior Monthly Settlement Cycle's Step 2 Capital and the price of SKY," implemented by Executive Vote.

The economics of the interim differ fundamentally from the target design even though the headline number looks similar. Rewards funded from *existing reserves* distribute tokens the protocol already holds; rewards funded from Step 3 buybacks are purchased on the market with revenue. The first is a drawdown, the second is a transfer of earnings. Only the second is sustainable, and only the second creates buy pressure.

Pegging the interim rate to 50% of prior-cycle Step 2 Capital is a smart bridge: stakers experience a payout that tracks protocol earnings, so the transition to the real mechanism should not feel like a change. Converting that figure through "the price of SKY" is where discretion enters — the same USD-equivalent implies a different token quantity at a different price, and that judgment is exercised monthly by the Core Facilitator.

The activation trigger is depletion-based rather than dated: A.2.3.1.4 says USDS Staking Rewards "become operational when the SKY tokens funding the Vesting Stream Contract approach depletion," as determined by the Core Facilitator with the Risk Advisor. The switch to revenue funding therefore happens when the reserve runs out, which ties a structural change to an exhaustion event rather than to readiness.
description: No Step 4 Capital funds SKY Staking Rewards yet; they come from Protocol Treasury reserves via a Vesting Stream Contract at a rate pegged to 50% of the prior cycle's Step 2 Capital.
